title: helm-hook-helpers-and-values-example-generator
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Introduce a reusable helm helper for hook conditionalization; add a small generator for values.yaml examples used in docs and e2e; tighten chart-testing workflow and add a step to lint hook templates; expose a canary_init_job toggle for safer upgrades.
description: Context: Private deployments have accumulated ad-hoc hook conditionals across multiple charts (private-installer, private-core, private-db). This causes subtle behavior divergence during upgrades/rollbacks and bloats templates. This PR centralizes hook decision logic into a chart helper and ships a small values-example generator that emits curated values.yaml snippets used in docs and in chart-tests. Motivation: make hook behavior consistent (init/cron/pre/post hooks), simplify templating, and provide deterministic example payloads that can be baked into release notes and upgrade playbooks. Summary of changes: - Add templates/_helpers/hook_helpers.tpl: a single entrypoint to evaluate whether to render a hook and which annotations to attach based on values (canaryInit, rollbackPolicy, atomicFallback). - Replace duplicated conditional blocks in charts/private-installer/templates/init-job.yaml and charts/private-core/templates/preupgrade-cron.yaml with calls to the helper. - Add tooling/dev/generate-values-examples.py: small script that reads values.schema.json and values.yaml and generates a set of annotated example snippets for docs and chart-tests. - Add values/examples/ canary and standard examples and wire them into docs build. - Extend chart-testing workflow: run helm template with --execute for hook resources and validate that no unexpected initJobs are created when canaryInit=false. - Add chart test fixture for an upgrade path that verifies hooks run only when canary toggle and rollbackPolicy are enabled. - Add docs/helm/hooks.md with examples and a short troubleshooting section for common upgrade failures. High-level commits: commit 1: introduce hook_helpers.tpl and unit tests for template logic; commit 2: refactor init/pre/post hook templates to use helper; commit 3: add generate-values-examples.py and CI step; commit 4: add docs and chart-tests; commit 5: fix CI lint failures for template indentation and re-run chart-tests. Files changed (high level): charts/private-installer/templates/init-job.yaml; charts/private-core/templates/preupgrade-cron.yaml; charts/private-db/templates/postupgrade-hook.yaml; charts/_helpers.tpl (new); values/examples/canary.yaml; values/examples/standard.yaml; tooling/generate-values-examples.py; .github/workflows/chart-testing.yml (updated); docs/helm/hooks.md. Important implementation notes: - The helper intentionally returns a tuple-like object through named labels (renderHook, hookAnnotation) encoded as a small line-delimited string to avoid nested dicts in templating. - generate-values-examples.py is deliberately small (no external deps beyond pyyaml used in CI) so it can be run in CI and locally by engineers. - The hook helper preserves existing annotation keys used by the private installer to signal the controller to wait for job completion; behavior is unchanged unless canaryInit is toggled. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is unchanged. The canary_init_job toggle is opt-in in values.yaml and off by default. This PR is not a breaking change. Testing and CI: - Initial push failed chart-testing due to helm-lint complaining about blank lines in helper comment blocks; fixed in subsequent commit. - chart-testing now runs helm template with an added --execute arg to validate hooks render as expected. - Unit tests added for template helper using helm unittest. Review/QA notes: Please pay attention to the helper contract (inputs: .Values.hooks.canaryInit, .Values.hooks.rollbackPolicy, .Release.Revision) and edge cases where rollbackPolicy="atomic" with canaryInit=true should still fall back to a safe path. Docs: hooks.md includes migration guidance for operators upgrading from older installers and a troubleshooting checklist used by Support when customers see stuck upgrades.
